interaction_type.value: dislocation accumulation at the δ-ferrite band / tempered martensite lamellar interfaces

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: During tensile tests, ductile deformation led to dislocation accumulation at the interfaces of δ-ferrite band and tempered martensite lamellar; due to the hardness difference between the two phases, stress concentration was prone to occur at their interfaces, inducing crack initiation. Cracks were captured by δ-ferrite and propagated into and along δ-ferrite band, forming second cracks; the crack could be blunted by the soft δ-ferrite phase, producing high resistance to cracking.

interface_notes.value: δ-ferrite and prior austenite grains grew up after the 1050 °C heating, and ferrite bands were segmented by martensite lamellar, becoming dispersed; this situation was kept in the annealed microstructure.

phase_evolution.value: After annealing, reverted austenite nucleated and grew up at martensite lath gaps; with increasing annealing temperature, increasingly reverted austenite nucleated and grew at the martensitic lath gaps, so block boundaries were gradually replaced by austenitic grain boundaries. In QA-680 no carbides precipitated (unlike QA-620).

slip_behavior.value: In stage I of work hardening, dislocation gliding started sequentially in ferrite and austenite as well as tempered martensite, according to the difference of phase hardness; large dislocation mean free path of ferrite caused the WHR to sharply decrease. Low GND density in tempered martensite promoted coordinate deformation between tempered martensite and δ-ferrite band.

source.reason: Discussion of interface cracking/second-crack formation at δ-ferrite/tempered martensite interfaces and phase evolution of reverted austenite; the QA condition description applies to the QA-680 state.
